en.title: Position of the First Character That Occurs Once
en.description:
Return the position of the earliest character among those that occur only once in the whole string, explicitly using 1-based positions; if there is none, output −1.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: One line with a lowercase string of length 1..100000.
en.explanation: Example 1: a is the earliest and occurs only once, at position 3. Example 2: both a and b repeat, so there is no unique character; output −1. Example 3: a is unique at position 2 and earlier than b, so output 2.
hints: First count the character frequencies, then find the first character with frequency 1 in the original order.
